notes.lead: The one deck they can do alone
notes.body: Hard or soft? needs no sound and marks itself, so it is the only deck in this unit a child can work through without you sitting there. Leave them to it.

cards.f: When is c hard, and when is it soft?
cards.m: Hard before a, o, u — casa, cosa, cura. Soft, like ch in chair, before e and i — cena, cinema.

cards.f: When is g hard, and when is it soft?
cards.m: Hard before a, o, u — gatto, gonna, gusto. Soft, like j in jam, before e and i — gelato, giro.

cards.f: What does an h do after c or g?
cards.m: Forces the hard sound back: chi, che, spaghetti, ghiaccio. The h itself is never pronounced.

cards.f: What does an i do after c or g, before a, o or u?
cards.m: Forces the soft sound: ciao, giornale. That i is not pronounced as a separate sound.
Hard — c before a.
Soft — c before e. CHE-na.
Hard — g before a.
Soft — g before e. je-LA-to.
Hard — the h keeps the c hard. KYEH-za.
Soft — the i makes the c soft, and is itself silent. chow.
Soft — c before i. CHEEN-kwe.
Hard — c before o.
Soft — the i makes the g soft, and is itself silent. JO-va-ne.
Hard — g before o.
Hard — the h keeps the g hard. GYAHT-cho.
Hard — the h keeps the c hard. KEE-lo.
Both. Hard cu, then soft ci. koo-CHEE-na.
Soft — the i makes the c soft, and is itself silent. chok-ko-LA-to.
Soft — g before i. MA-ji-ko.
Hard — the h keeps the g hard. spa-GET-tee.
